# Go data-access libraries for Amarra — study

**Date:** 2026-09-24
**Status:** Recommendation — do not adopt a runtime ORM in the framework or default scaffold
**Scope:** Evaluate Go ORMs / query compilers for `pkg/cais` internals and for apps generated by `amarra-cais new` / `g resource` / `g model`
**Non-goal:** Implement a library in this document. This is the decision record.

---

## Goal

Decide whether Amarra should add an ORM (or ORM-adjacent layer) so generated stores stop hand-writing `Query`/`Scan`, without breaking the contracts that already ship:

- Pure-Go SQLite (`modernc.org/sqlite`, no CGO)
- SQL files as the schema source of truth (`-- up` / `-- down`)
- `pkg/cais/migrate` on boot
- `sqllog.Wrap` on the app `*sql.DB`
- `sqlite.Configure`: WAL, `busy_timeout=5000`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `MaxOpenConns(1)`
- `:memory:` store tests, no mocked DB
- `Store.DB() *sql.DB` for jobs, sessions, `/jobs`
- Generators that emit greppable SQL inside `internal/store`

---

## Current contract

The framework is **SQL-first already**. There is no ORM today, by design.

| Layer               | Access                            | Notes                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Generated app store | `database/sql` via `*sqllog.DB`   | `internal/cli/tpl_scaffold_store.go`, `resource_gen_store.go`                                                                   |
| Migrations          | `.sql` files + `pkg/cais/migrate` | Markers `-- up` / `-- down`                                                                                                     |
| Jobs                | `*sql.DB`                         | `pkg/cais/jobs` — same file as the app                                                                                          |
| Sessions            | `*sql.DB`                         | `pkg/cais/session`                                                                                                              |
| SQL logs            | wrapper around `*sql.DB`          | `sqllog.Wrap` — `Exec` / `Query` / `QueryRow` plus `*Context` variants; short methods delegate to `context.Background()` (#264) |
| Driver              | `modernc.org/sqlite`              | DSN pragmas in `pkg/cais/sqlite.DSN`                                                                                            |

Generated CRUD is already explicit SQL:

```go
s.db.QueryRow("SELECT id, %s, created_at FROM %s WHERE id = ?", id).Scan(...)
s.db.Query("SELECT ... FROM %s"+where+" ORDER BY "+orderCol+" "+orderDir+" LIMIT ? OFFSET ?", args...)
```

List endpoints whitelist `sort`/`dir` in Go (`OrderClause`) and concatenate the column name after the whitelist. That dynamic `ORDER BY` is the hardest query shape for compile-time SQL tools.

`sqllog.DB` is **not** a `*sql.DB`. It implements `ExecContext` / `QueryContext` / `QueryRowContext` so sqlc's `DBTX` can sit on `s.db`. `PrepareContext` and `BeginTx` are still absent if generated code needs them.

---

## Candidates (2026)

Sources: official docs and current project pages, not blog ranking scores.

| Library                                                                       | Kind                                    | Stars (approx.) | Runtime dep?                   | Codegen?              | SQLite / no-CGO                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [sqlc](https://docs.sqlc.dev/en/latest/tutorials/getting-started-sqlite.html) | SQL → typed Go                          | ~18k            | No (stdlib `database/sql`)     | Yes (`sqlc generate`) | First-class `engine: sqlite`; tutorial uses `modernc.org/sqlite`. sqlc CLI itself dropped CGO in [v1.25.0](https://sqlc.dev/posts/2024/01/04/sqlc-v1-25-0-c-ya-c-go/) |
| [Bun](https://bun.uptrace.dev/guide/drivers.html)                             | SQL-first ORM / query builder           | ~5k             | Yes (`github.com/uptrace/bun`) | No                    | Wraps `*sql.DB`. `sqliteshim` picks modernc by default; dialect docs say SQLite pool **MaxOpenConns(1)**                                                              |
| [Ent](https://entgo.io/docs/dialects)                                         | Schema-in-Go entity framework           | ~17k            | Yes + large generated tree     | Yes (`ent generate`)  | Official tutorials use `mattn/go-sqlite3` (CGO). Can take a custom `*sql.DB`. Migrations via Atlas                                                                    |
| [GORM](https://gorm.io)                                                       | Full runtime ORM                        | ~40k            | Yes                            | No                    | Official `gorm.io/driver/sqlite` is CGO (`mattn/go-sqlite3`). Pure-Go path is community (`glebarez/sqlite` last tagged v1.11.0 / GORM 1.25.7; `libtnb/sqlite`)        |
| [sqlx](https://github.com/jmoiron/sqlx)                                       | `database/sql` helpers (`Get`/`Select`) | ~18k            | Yes                            | No                    | Driver-agnostic. Last release **v1.4.0 (2024-04)**; maintenance is slow                                                                                               |
| squirrel / go-jet                                                             | Query builders                          | —               | Yes                            | jet: yes              | Driver-agnostic; still emit SQL strings                                                                                                                               |

Community writing in 2026 (Encore, sqlc vs GORM vs sqlx comparisons) describes a shift toward **SQL-first / codegen** (sqlc, Bun) and away from reflection ORMs for new work. That matches Amarra's generators: they already emit SQL, they do not emit entity graphs.

---

## Constraint matrix

A library that cannot satisfy a row is out as the **default**.

| Constraint                                                 | sqlc                                                                                                       | Bun                                                                                                                                   | Ent                                                     | GORM                                              | sqlx               | stay `database/sql` |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------- |
| No CGO / `modernc.org/sqlite`                              | Yes (official tutorial)                                                                                    | Yes if we open modernc ourselves and pass `*sql.DB` (avoid relying on `sqliteshim` swapping drivers)                                  | Possible via custom `*sql.DB`; docs/examples are CGO    | Official driver is CGO; extra community dialector | Yes                | Yes                 |
| Keep SQL file migrations + `pkg/cais/migrate`              | Yes — sqlc **does not migrate**; it only parses schema                                                     | Has its own migrator; can be ignored                                                                                                  | Atlas / `Schema.Create` fights our runner               | `AutoMigrate` fights our runner                   | Yes                | Yes                 |
| Keep `sqllog.Wrap`                                         | Yes — `*Context` on `sqllog.DB`/`Tx` (#264). `PrepareContext` / `BeginTx` still missing if sqlc emits them | Logs via Bun hooks **or** wrap `*sql.DB` before `bun.NewDB`                                                                           | Own logger; bypasses `sqllog` unless we wrap the driver | Own logger; same                                  | Can wrap `*sql.DB` | Yes                 |
| `MaxOpenConns(1)` + WAL + busy_timeout                     | Unchanged (we still `sql.Open`)                                                                            | Compatible if we configure the underlying `*sql.DB`                                                                                   | Compatible if we configure the underlying `*sql.DB`     | Easy to lose if `gorm.Open` owns the pool         | Yes                | Yes                 |
| `:memory:` tests                                           | Yes                                                                                                        | Shim examples use `SetMaxIdleConns(1000)` for in-memory — **conflicts** with our `MaxOpenConns(1)` unless we keep our DSN/`Configure` | Yes with care                                           | Yes with care                                     | Yes                | Yes                 |
| `Store.DB() *sql.DB` for jobs/session/`jobsui`             | Yes — sqlc sits on `DBTX`                                                                                  | Yes — `db.DB` is the `*sql.DB`                                                                                                        | Yes if we keep the raw DB                               | Awkward (`*gorm.DB` is the unit)                  | Yes                | Yes                 |
| Dynamic `ORDER BY` after column whitelist (resource index) | Awkward — SQL must be static; `CASE WHEN` per column or keep a raw helper                                  | Natural (query builder)                                                                                                               | Predicates, not string concat                           | `Order(sort + " " + dir)` still needs a whitelist | Same as today      | Natural             |
| Agent / grep (unique SQL, small files, no magic)           | Strong — queries live in `.sql`                                                                            | Medium — builder chains                                                                                                               | Weak — generated `ent/` tree, graph API                 | Weak — callbacks, associations, `AutoMigrate`     | Strong             | Strong              |
| Extra tool in `amarra-cais new` / CI                       | `sqlc` CLI + `sqlc.yaml`                                                                                   | Go module only                                                                                                                        | `ent` CLI + `go generate`                               | Go module + dialector                             | Go module          | None                |
| Parse our `-- up` / `-- down` files as schema              | **No** — sqlc understands goose, dbmate, golang-migrate, atlas, sql-migrate, tern. Our markers are custom  | N/A                                                                                                                                   | N/A                                                     | N/A                                               | N/A                | Yes                 |

Hard rejects as the **default scaffold / framework dep**:

1. **GORM** — official SQLite driver is CGO; `AutoMigrate` becomes a second schema source; associations/hooks are the opposite of greppable store methods; `sqllog` would not see queries unless we abandon it for GORM's logger.
2. **Ent** — schema-in-Go replaces SQL migrations as the source of truth; Atlas vs `pkg/cais/migrate`; generated package is large; official SQLite examples are CGO; graph/entity model is heavier than `g resource` CRUD.
3. **Putting any ORM inside `pkg/cais/jobs`, `session`, or `migrate`** — those packages must stay on `*sql.DB`. Jobs already share the file with WAL + single writer. An ORM pool or AutoMigrate there is a production footgun.

---

## Approaches

### A — Keep `database/sql` (recommended default)

Generated stores stay as they are: `Store` interface, `SQLiteStore`, SQL strings, `Scan`, whitelist for sort.

**Pros**

- Zero new runtime or CLI dependency in every app
- Matches AGENTS.md, doctor, smoke scaffold, and `:memory:` tests
- SQL is already greppable in `internal/store`
- Framework packages (`jobs`, `session`, `migrate`, `sqllog`) stay a single style

**Cons**

- `Scan` argument lists grow with each field (`resource_gen_store.go` already has declare/assign helpers)
- Typos in SQL surface at request time, not `go test` compile of a generated query package
- Agents copy the same Query/Scan boilerplate

**When this is enough:** it already is, for the CRUD Amarra generates (insert/update/delete/find/list/count/seed).

### B — sqlc for **generated app** stores only (recommended upgrade if we add anything)

Framework stays `database/sql`. `amarra-cais g resource` / `g model` would emit:

```
internal/store/migrations/*.sql     # still applied by pkg/cais/migrate
internal/store/queries/*.sql        # sqlc input
sqlc.yaml
internal/store/sqlc/                # generated, do not edit
internal/store/store.go             # Store interface wrapping sqlc.Queries
```

sqlc's own SQLite tutorial opens `modernc.org/sqlite` and uses `database/sql`. Generated code talks to a `DBTX` interface (`ExecContext` / `QueryContext` / `QueryRowContext`). Runtime dependency of the app stays stdlib + modernc.

**Pros**

- Compile-time check that queries match schema
- Scan boilerplate disappears
- SQL stays the source of truth (same philosophy as migrations)
- No ORM session, no hooks, no AutoMigrate
- sqlc CLI is CGO-free since 1.25.0
- Agents write `.sql` files (they are already good at SQL)

**Cons / work we would owe**

1. **`PrepareContext` / `BeginTx`.** `sqllog.DB`/`Tx` now log `ExecContext` / `QueryContext` / `QueryRowContext` (#264). sqlc's full `DBTX` also wants `PrepareContext`; transactional sqlc wants `BeginTx`. Add them if generated code needs them.
2. **Migration markers.** sqlc will not skip our `-- down` sections. Options: emit a `schema.sql` from up-sections for sqlc; or add goose-style `-- +goose Up` **in addition to** `-- up` (keep `pkg/cais/migrate` as the runner); or teach a tiny adapter. Do not replace `pkg/cais/migrate`.
3. **Dynamic `ORDER BY`.** Resource indexes pass `sort`/`dir` from the query string. sqlc wants static SQL. Keep `OrderClause` + a small raw `Query` for `List*` / `ListAll*`, or expand `ORDER BY CASE WHEN @sort = 'title' THEN title END` per column. Do not interpolate untrusted identifiers into sqlc SQL.
4. **CI / doctor.** `sqlc generate` must run in app CI and `amarra-cais doctor` should fail if generated files are stale.
5. **Two model types.** sqlc emits its own structs. Either `emit_db_models` into `internal/models` carefully, or map sqlc rows → existing `models.X` in the store wrapper so handlers stay unchanged.

**Out of scope for B:** rewriting jobs, sessions, or the framework itself in sqlc.

### C — Bun as a query builder on the existing `*sql.DB`

Open modernc + `sqlite.Configure` + `sqllog` as today, then `bun.NewDB(raw, sqlitedialect.New())` for app CRUD only.

**Pros**

- Dynamic `WHERE` / `ORDER BY` / pagination are natural
- Can still run raw SQL
- SQLite dialect exists; we can refuse `sqliteshim` and keep our driver pin

**Cons**

- Runtime ORM in every generated `go.mod`
- Struct tags (`bun:"..."`) become a second schema
- Temptation to use Bun migrations / fixtures / soft delete — we would have to forbid them in AGENTS.md
- Agents generate builder chains that are harder to grep than SQL files
- In-memory examples in Bun docs fight `MaxOpenConns(1)`

Bun is the least-bad **runtime** ORM if someone insists on a builder. It is still the wrong default for a framework whose generators already write SQL.

---

## Recommendation

**Do not add GORM, Ent, Bun, or sqlx to `pkg/cais` or to `amarra-cais new`.**

The default data layer stays:

```
modernc.org/sqlite → sqlite.Configure / DSN
                   → pkg/cais/migrate
                   → sqllog.Wrap
                   → store.SQLiteStore (database/sql)
                   → Store.DB() for jobs + sessions
```

That is not an unfinished ORM. It is the product: one SQLite file, SQL migrations, greppable queries, headless tests.

**If we invest in typed queries later, the only library that fits is sqlc, and only in generated apps (Approach B).** Ship it behind a generator flag (`amarra-cais new --sqlc` / `g resource` emitting `queries/*.sql`) after `sqllog` grows Context methods. Keep `List*` sort/dir as a whitelist helper until sqlc has a clean static pattern we are willing to emit.

**sqlx** is a possible micro-step to shrink `Scan` lines (`StructScan`) without codegen. It does not check SQL, adds a slow-moving dependency, and is optional per-app — not a framework feature.

---

## What generated SQL would look like under B (sketch)

Today the generator writes Go. Under sqlc it would write:

```sql
-- name: InsertBookmark :execlastid
INSERT INTO bookmarks (title, url, notes)
VALUES (?, ?, ?);

-- name: FindBookmarkByID :one
SELECT id, title, url, notes, created_at
FROM bookmarks
WHERE id = ?;

-- name: DeleteBookmark :exec
DELETE FROM bookmarks WHERE id = ?;
```

`ListBookmarks` with search + sort stays in Go (whitelist + concat) **or** becomes a `CASE` sort. The `Store` interface does not change, so handlers keep calling `h.store.ListBookmarks(...)`.

---

## Key decisions

| Decision                                             | Rationale                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No runtime ORM in `pkg/cais`                         | Jobs, sessions, migrate, and sqllog are `*sql.DB` contracts; an ORM pool or AutoMigrate would split the schema and break WAL/`MaxOpenConns(1)` assumptions |
| No ORM in default `amarra-cais new`                  | Smoke scaffold, doctor, and AGENTS.md all assume SQL files + `SQLiteStore`                                                                                 |
| Reject GORM and Ent as defaults                      | CGO official SQLite paths, second migration engine, generated/magic APIs that fight agent grep                                                             |
| sqlc is the only upgrade path worth a later PR       | SQL-first, `database/sql`, official modernc tutorial, no runtime ORM                                                                                       |
| Keep `-- up` / `-- down` + `pkg/cais/migrate`        | Do not switch to goose/Atlas just to please sqlc; adapt schema input if we add sqlc                                                                        |
| Dynamic sort stays a Go whitelist                    | Untrusted `?sort=` must never be concatenated into sqlc SQL without the existing allow-list                                                                |
| `sqllog` Context methods are a prerequisite for sqlc | Done for `ExecContext` / `QueryContext` / `QueryRowContext` (#264). `PrepareContext` / `BeginTx` remain if sqlc emits them                                 |

---

## Open questions

None blocking this recommendation. Resolve only if we start Approach B:

1. **Flag vs default** — `amarra-cais new --sqlc` forever, or become default after one minor version of opt-in?
2. **sqlc version pin** — ship as `tool` in the app `go.mod` vs document `go install github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@vX`.
3. **`List*` implementation** — keep raw SQL helper vs emit per-column `CASE` sorts.
